subject: Discovery recap — TCO scenarios, token economics & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — TCO scenarios, token economics & next steps

Thanks again for a productive conversation earlier today, Samantha — appreciate you carving out time. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key pain points, proposed saving levers, and a concrete set of next steps so your procurement and engineering teams can align.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary pain: inference cost variability and unpredictable latency during batch scoring windows for edge fleet telemetry. Current vendor billing spikes ~3x during peak uploads.
- Goals: 1) reduce monthly inference spend while keeping 99th pct latency under 300ms for critical alerts, 2) enable cost predictability for quarterly budgeting, 3) a plan to run a 6-week proof-of-value on a representative workload.
- Constraints: existing VPC/VPN requirements, requirement for audit logs, and a target pilot budget cap of $15k/month for the POC phase.

TCO / token-economics assumptions we discussed (see attached spreadsheet for line-item math)
- Baseline: Acme estimates 700M tokens/month for scoring + 120M prompt tokens across models today. Current blended cost estimate (per their vendor invoice) ~ $0.009/token effective.
- Redwood hosted baseline pricing: conservative run-rate estimate (no batching/caching) ~ $0.0045/token effective.
- Batching & caching levers: expected reductions by combining continuous batching and prefix KV caching:
  • Batching: reduces per-token compute by ~18–28% for median request size (we model 22% here).
  • KV/prefix caching: re-use on repeated telemetry patterns — conservative hit rate 12%, upside to 25% for steady-state.
- Modeled pilot outcome (6 weeks) — conservative scenario:
  • Projected tokens processed: 120M tokens (pilot sample)
  • Projected effective cost with Redwood + batching/caching: $0.0032/token -> ~ $384k annualized run-rate equivalent for same volume; for pilot sample ~ $384 (scaled numbers in sheet).
  • Budget fit: with burst caps and committed capacity, we can keep pilot costs under your $15k/month cap with auto-fallback to smaller models during peak ingestion.

Risk & remediation
- Latency risk on cold-cache startup: mitigated by warmup runs and pre-loading hot KV prefixes before peak windows.
- Security/compliance: private deployment (VPC) + audit logs + KMS integration in scope for the POC.

Next steps (proposed; please confirm who from your side for procurement and infra)
1) Redwood provides sandbox access + sample bundle (3 model variants + pre-configured batching profile) — target provisioning by Fri 6/12.
2) Technical deep-dive with Acme infra (30–45m) to walk the sample runbook and network requirements (Marissa to lead).
3) Provide a two-scenario TCO estimate in the spreadsheet: (A) conservative hit rates, (B) optimistic hit rates (Grace to produce).
4) Procurement checklist: draft contract and SOW placeholder for a 6-week POC; legal/procurement review kickoff on 6/17 if feasible.

Attachments: 20260610-acme-tco-scenarios.xlsx (cost model), redwood-sample-sla.pdf

Appreciate any corrections/notes and who should be the point for procurement. Happy to jump on another quick sync if you prefer a walkthrough of the spreadsheet.

—
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — TCO scenarios, token economics & next steps

Jordan — great write-up, thank you. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the assumptions: 

1) Volume check: the 700M tokens/month is our current peak estimate across all fleets; for the pilot we want a 10% sample (~70M tokens/month) to validate latency and caching effectiveness. Please show a 70M pilot scenario in the conservative tab.

2) Budget: procurement confirms the POC budget cap is firm at $15k/month but we can reallocate some infra credits for the pilot. Any line items that depend on reserved capacity vs burst pricing should be highlighted.

3) Security: security will need SOC2 attestation and vault-backed key management for model keys; can you confirm Redwood supports customer-managed keys in the Private deployment? Also need a list of audit log fields we can forward to our compliance team.

4) Timeline: procurement prefers contract/PO by 6/25 to start the pilot end of June. Legal will review T&Cs; we'll share a redline turn time expectation (3 business days) if possible.

I can be the exec sponsor for this POC; Kevin (procurement@acme.ai) will own contracts. Please add Marissa’s deep-dive session to our calendar.

Thanks —
Samantha
Head of ML Ops, Acme Robotics
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — TCO scenarios, token economics & next steps

Thanks Samantha — all clear and aligns with what we discussed. Quick answers inline: 

- 70M pilot scenario: noted — Grace will add a dedicated 70M conservative/optimistic tab and include per-day ramp profile so we can size reserved vs burst.
- Reserved vs burst: we'll show two costing columns: (A) hosted burst pricing, (B) 3-month reserved capacity with predictable monthly commit. Typically reserved gives ~28–33% unit cost reduction for steady-state traffic.
- Customer-managed keys: yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integration and we can supply the KMS integration checklist for your security team.
- Audit logs: we will export request-id, model-version, route, token-count, latency-ms, and requester-id for the pilot; will include sample schema in the technical deep-dive.
- Timeline: aiming to provision sandbox by 6/12; contract/PO by 6/25 is workable.

Action owners / near-term commitments
- Grace O'Connor: produce updated spreadsheet with 70M pilot tab + reserved vs burst columns (ETA 6/12 EOD).
- Marissa Cole: schedule technical deep-dive with Samantha/Acme infra — propose Mon 6/15 or Tue 6/16.
- Jordan Blake: provide SOW placeholder and sample SLA; loop in legal for initial redlines (ETA 6/12).

I'll attach the sample SLA and one-page SOW in the follow-up. If procurement needs a budget line for committed capacity vs burst, Kevin, let us know preferred display (monthly vs quarterly).

—
Jordan
From: Kevin Morales <procurement@acme.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — TCO scenarios, token economics & next steps

Jordan/Marissa — procurement quick note: please include the following in the SOW/quote to speed PO approval:
- Clear definition of trial scope in tokens and time (we need the 70M tokens / 6-week window clearly stated).
- Billing cap clause for pilot not to exceed $15k/month unless pre-approved in writing.
- Contact points for support/escalation and expected SLAs during pilot window.

If you can email a draft quote and SOW today I’ll start internal routing so legal can be looped in tomorrow.

Thanks,
